author: GamingBolt
description:
End of Abyss isn't a horrible experience overall, and there are some bright spots where you settle into a groove, retrieving keys and returning to previous locations to progress. Running into a dead end and having to scan, whether it's something on a corpse nearby or a vent, to progress is also neat. 

And if I haven't emphasised it already, the art direction is fairly gorgeous. As confined as the Facility feels, it has an impressive sense of scale, especially when traversing walkways above previous sections or encountering the giant reactor for the first time. It's just that the core gameplay elements intentionally get in the way and drag the whole thing down. 

The combination of genres and approaches ultimately feels at odds with the experience, almost like End of Abyss isn't sure what it wants to be, and ultimately falters as a result.
title: End of Abyss Review - The Final Verdict

author: GamingBolt
description:
The sheer scale of The Witcher 3: Remastered means I've forgotten so much, but the overall feel and atmosphere, that pull to explore, hearing “Wind's howling” before the inevitable rains follow, and meeting these beloved characters once again, is undeniable. 

Of course, the gameplay improvements certainly don't hurt, whether it's the combat animations, new finishers, transmog or the dozens of other quality-of-life features.

Which is why I hope CD Projekt RED addresses the many bugs and performance concerns as quickly as possible. I didn't really need the remaster in my life, even without the deluge of critically-acclaimed titles lately, my backlog is enough to keep me busy for the next year. But if there's ever a time to return to The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, especially with Songs of the Past coming up, it's now. And a fairly well-polished welcome mat certainly wouldn't hurt.
title: Why The Witcher 3: Remastered Is So Hard To Put Down?

author: GamingBolt
description:
GTA 6 gets bigger with every passing day, and every new piece of news we learn about it. It’s an ambitious effort from a franchise that’s been around forever, and Rockstar seems to be sparing no effort to give the behemoth its due.

New information is available and we thought you’d like to know what’s coming to the title you’re likely planning to add to your library. We’ve got you covered, so join us as we look at a few things about Leonidas that could make it worth your while to jump right in with the rest of us when GTA 6 finally drops after an interminably long wait.
title: GTA 6 - 15 NEW Features You Need To Know Before You Buy (Part 3)
